name: Toast
purpose: A Sonner-style stacking notification, fixed to the top-right corner, triggered imperatively (toast.success('Saved')) from anywhere — not tied to a piece of UI state the consumer renders conditionally, unlike Modal/SidePanel.
neverUseFor: A message the user must act on before continuing — use Modal instead, Toast can be missed or auto-dismiss
Form field validation errors — show them inline next to the field, not as a Toast
Anything the user needs to refer back to later — Toast auto-dismisses and doesn't persist

anatomy.description: Fixed, top-right, portaled to document.body via createPortal (ADR-011). Rendered by the <Toast /> component, mounted once by the consuming app.
One notification. Background is always the page fill — color lives only on the icon, never the card (ADR-011), a deliberate difference from Badge's own tinted-surface convention.
A real Filled Tabler icon through the Icon component, fixed per variant — not caller-supplied like Badge's own icon prop.
An IconButton (IconX) that dismisses this toast early.

width.note: Fixed viewport/card width, not on the shared size scale — same category of per-component literal as SidePanel's width.

a11y.role: each toast-viewport region uses aria-live="polite" so screen readers announce new toasts without interrupting; toast-close is a real button with an accessible label
keyboardNav: Tab reaches each visible toast's close button
Hovering (mouse) pauses auto-dismiss and pauses no keyboard-equivalent yet — see ADR-011's open item on this
notes: Triggered via the imperative `toast` object (toast.success/info/warning/danger/neutral(label, description?)), not props on <Toast /> itself — see ADR-011. <Toast /> is the rendered stack, mounted once; it takes almost no props of its own.

Stacking depth (max 3 visible) and hover-to-spread use real measured pixel heights (offsetHeight), not percentage-based transforms — a percentage approach was tried and broken in the pre-implementation preview by two toasts of different heights; see ADR-011.
